approval.trigger: REST API tokens: no review of any kind; a user generates a token and it works. Pack Gallery publishing: Coda's official help article describes a self-serve flow (completed listing page + at least one released version, then Publish) with no review step, timeline, or eligibility thresholds. One real approval gate exists inside Packs: the 'Custom' authentication type requires support approval ('Contact support to request approval'), with no stated timeline.
approval.wait: None stated for tokens or Gallery publishing; Custom-auth approval duration not stated

blockers.detail: There is no OAuth app registration, client ID/secret for the Coda API, or consent flow in Coda's official documentation. No delegated consent, no scopes, no refresh tokens: your onboarding is 'ask the user to generate and paste a token', a long-lived credential the user manages manually, or meeting users inside Coda via a Pack. Third-party blogs describe coda.io/oauth2 endpoints; no official Coda documentation supports them, so treat them as non-existent.
blockers.howToClear: Choose the token-paste UX or the Pack route deliberately, and be transparent with users about the credential they are handing over.
blockers.title: The missing OAuth flow is the blocker

blockers.detail: Packs execute on Coda's platform via its fetcher; 'Packs don't have direct access to the user's credentials', and only a fixed set of authentication types is supported: 'it's not possible to write completely custom authentication code'. If your product is an external backend, the Pack model may not fit at all.
blockers.howToClear: Evaluate the Pack execution model against your architecture before committing; the REST token path is the external-backend option.
blockers.title: Packs run inside Coda, not in your backend

tested: Read-only verification: the absence of any OAuth app/consent mechanism for the Coda API, the API-token model, and the Pack auth types were checked against current coda.io developer documentation and help articles (no token generated, no Pack created)
unverified: Whether API tokens can be scoped or restricted (e.g. to a single doc, or read-only): not confirmed from an official page read in this pass.
API token expiry/lifetime (not stated in the docs read).
Whether Gallery publishing involves human review in practice (the help article describes none; absence in one article is not proof).
Cost/monetization review requirements for paid Packs (not covered).
The third-party-claimed coda.io/oauth2/* endpoints: unverifiable in official docs and treated as non-existent for this guide.

alternatives: A Pack using CodaApiHeaderBearerToken with shouldAutoAuthSetup: true (the token is automatically created with default settings when the Pack is installed; the smoothest 'connect' experience for Coda data, inside Coda)
flavor.recommended: No OAuth flavor exists. For the REST API: a per-user API token your customer generates in their Coda account settings and pastes into your product (sent as Authorization: Bearer)
flavor.why: Coda's official docs contain no OAuth app registration or consent flow for third-party access to Coda data. OAuth2 exists in the Packs SDK only in the OUTBOUND direction (your Pack connecting to other services like GitHub, using your credentials for that provider). For Coda's own API, the credential object is the API token.

humanMust: Each user generates their own API token in Coda account settings (API settings) and pastes it into your product
Pack route: release a version and complete the listing in Pack Studio
Users install the Pack and click 'Connect an account' if you ship a Pack
name: Coda
nuances: Outbound Pack OAuth supports only the Authorization Code and Client Credentials grant types; providers that deviate too far from standard OAuth 2.0 may not be configurable at all. Token-exchange client authentication is tried automatically in both common variants (secret in body, or Basic header), with no configuration and no control.
System authentication in a Pack means all users share the MAKER's credentials: fine for public-data APIs, wrong for per-user private data.

If your Pack connects to a third party that verifies OAuth apps (e.g. Google), the Packs FAQ says getting the Pack verified by that provider 'may take a week or more', with the platform's fixed redirect URL on Coda's domain as a common friction point.
Coda's docs are mid-rebrand: the same documentation says 'Superhuman Docs/Packs SDK' interchangeably with Coda, and API examples point at docs.superhuman.com. Expect branding inconsistency.

Workspace/organization admins can restrict Pack sharing and publishing via sharing policies (e.g. 'No external sharing'), so enterprise users may be blocked from installing your Pack by their own admin settings.
prerequisites: REST path: a token-entry form and secure credential storage in your product
Pack path: the Packs CLI and a Coda API token for uploads

steps.detail: Instruct the user: sign in to Coda > Account settings > API settings > Generate API token (name it, copy it). There is no developer portal step for you at all.
steps.title: (REST path) User generates an API token

steps.detail: The user pastes the token into your product; you store it securely and call coda.io/apis/v1 with Authorization: Bearer <token> (e.g. GET /apis/v1/whoami identifies the user).
steps.title: (REST path) Store the token and call the API

steps.detail: Scaffold with the Packs CLI (register an upload token, packs create), then declare setUserAuthentication({ type: CodaApiHeaderBearerToken, shouldAutoAuthSetup: true }) so a Superhuman Docs API token is created automatically at install. For third-party services instead, declare OAuth2 with that provider's URLs/scopes and store your client ID/secret in the Pack's Settings tab.
steps.title: (Pack path) Build a Pack with Coda token auth

steps.detail: In Pack Studio: Build > Release at least one version (with release notes), complete the Listing tab, then Share > Publish tab > Publish to the Coda Gallery, or share with specific workspaces. End users install the Pack into a doc and click 'Connect an account'; with auto-auth setup the token is created during sign-in.
steps.title: (Pack path) Release and publish

tagline: There is no OAuth app to create for Coda's API: users hand you an API token, or you meet them inside Coda as a Pack whose Coda token is auto-created at install. OAuth in the Packs SDK points the other way, at other services.

time.active: Minutes for the token path; ~half a day to build and release a Pack
time.total: Same day either way; no review stands in front of users
